summary: Implement Issue #1 kernel lifecycle: every protocol/startup/dispose terminal transition kills and evicts the owning process tree, waitReady is bounded by the eval deadline and caller AbortSignal, Runtime.dispose() is idempotent-terminal so post-dispose eval rejects without spawning.

pointers: M2: a corrupt JSON frame from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: a non-object frame from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: an unknown frame type from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: a frame with a wrong request id from the kernel kills and evicts the process tree
M2: a wrong ready version terminates the startup path once, kills, and evicts
M2: a silent kernel that never sends ready is killed by the startup deadline
M2: aborting during the ready handshake kills the kernel and rejects with cancel
M2: disposing during the ready handshake settles the waiter and kills the kernel
M2: dispose is terminal and a later eval is rejected without spawning

steps: Read AGENTS.md, issue-repair-playbook.md, architecture.md, milestones.md, project-status.md, review-findings.md, development-memory README and the existing runtime/tests/kernel before mutating; reference decision for host-side lifecycle is mechanism-absent (no local ref/rlm or ref/prime-agent source checkout exists).

Reproduced all three defects on the frozen base with a temp script: protocol fault left the kernel PID alive (orphan kept the Node event loop open), a 400ms timeout did not bound a silent ready wait, and eval after dispose still attempted a spawn (kind=spawn).

Implemented unified terminal transitions: Kernel.handleExit now always kills the process tree before onExit eviction; Kernel.waitReady races the ready promise against the effective cell timeout and the caller AbortSignal through handleExit; Kernel.dispose rejects a pending ready and marks exited; RlmRuntimeImpl is terminal after dispose so eval rejects closed without spawning; ready version mismatch was rerouted through handleExit.

Added deterministic regression tests: raw-frame injection through sys.__stdout__ for corrupt JSON/non-object/unknown frame/wrong request id, sitecustomize-shadowed silent startup for ready deadline/abort/dispose plus bad ready version, and a terminal-dispose test with a missing interpreter; every lifecycle test asserts the real OS PID is gone via tasklist.
Ran pnpm typecheck, pnpm build, focused tests and the full offline suite before staging the candidate.

evidence.note: Protocol-fault PID stayed alive, ready wait did not settle within 1.5s under a 400ms timeout, and eval after dispose attempted spawn (kind=spawn) — all three defects reproduced on the frozen base.
tsc emit plus tsdown produced lib/index.mjs.

37/37 tests pass, including corrupt JSON, non-object, unknown frame, wrong request id, bad ready version, silent ready deadline, ready abort, ready dispose and terminal dispose; each lifecycle test asserts the real kernel PID disappeared.
45 tests: 43 pass, 2 skipped (RLM_LIVE_SMOKE-gated profile smoke), 0 fail.

limitations: The ready startup deadline reuses the effective cell timeout (input.timeout ?? config.timeout) as its own budget; startup and cell execution are not charged against one shared deadline and no separate startup-timeout option was added.

Protocol-fault coverage drives the host parser by having a cell write raw frames through sys.__stdout__; the unmodified production kernel never emits malformed frames, so these tests validate host defensive behavior only.

Silent-startup coverage shadows sitecustomize through PYTHONPATH with a PID marker; it depends on Python importing sitecustomize during interpreter startup and on the Windows-specific tasklist PID probes already used by the suite.

The synchronous-throw spawn() path (for example a non-executable interpreter command) still settles via rejectReady without the unified handleExit eviction; it predates this Issue and is out of scope.
No clean-Profile live smoke was run for this candidate (RLM_LIVE_SMOKE not set); lifecycle acceptance is proven by the deterministic offline suite only.
